challenge.description: Early summer brings the meiyu — weeks of warm, unrelenting rain. The paddies flood, stored food molds, mosquitoes rise in clouds, and the rivers take back their roads.
challenge.name: The Plum Rains

seasons.note: Greens return. Bamboo shoots push up — the hungry season's exit.
The plum rains, then typhoon season. Hot, wet, everything grows — including the mosquitoes.
Harvest. Persimmons, chestnuts, rice. Fatten up.
The Siberian wind. Dry, bitter, still. Stored food or nothing.

covers: Eastern China, the Korean peninsula, Japan: bamboo brakes, feral rice paddies, persimmon orchards, tea terraces gone wild

bamboo brake: Where the poles stand thick, the shoots come up sweet.
chestnut lane: The burrs split in fall. Watch your fingers; the nuts are worth it.
feral paddy: The paddies went wild years ago. The rice didn't get the memo.
goji hedge: Thorny hedges, red berries. The birds know.
mulberry row: Silkworm country, once. The berries are for whoever's hungry now.
old orchard: Someone planted food here once. The trees remember.
pond margin: Still water, broad leaves standing tall. Dinner is under the mud.
tea terrace: Terraces gone to seed. The bushes still flush every spring.
temple ginkgo: Planted for shade and long life. The nuts are a bonus — roast them, and mind the dose.
wet ditch: Crisp corms under the mud. Cook them — the ditch water isn't clean.

name: East Asia

ruins: An elementary school. The classrooms are open to the sky; a wall chart of the seasons still hangs, faded to pastels. Someone chalked a height chart on a doorframe — the marks stop halfway up.

A township clinic. The medicine cabinet was emptied years ago, but the posters on the wall still explain hand-washing in four cheerful steps. The examination table is now a planter — mugwort grows through it.
A bus depot. The buses sit in a patient row, tires long since gone to moss. The route map by the gate is still legible: forty stops, none of which exist anymore.
A small roadside shrine, roofed and swept — someone still tends it. The offering box is empty, and stays empty.

scavenge.name: Instant noodles
scavenge.text: A brick of noodles, seasoning dust at the bottom of the bag. Civilization's emergency ration.

scavenge.name: Canned congee
scavenge.text: Rice porridge in a can. Bland, warm, perfect — the taste of being looked after.

scavenge.name: Rice cakes
scavenge.text: Pounded rice, dried hard. Soak it, grill it, soup it — it keeps coming back.

scavenge.name: Dried seaweed
scavenge.text: Nori sheets, still crisp. Salt and iodine in paper-thin form.

scavenge.name: Canned mackerel
scavenge.text: Oily fish in a tin. The bones went soft years ago; the flavor didn't.

scavenge.name: Soy sauce
scavenge.text: A heavy bottle, half full. Salt you can pour — everything bland becomes food again.

scavenge.name: Mooncakes (lotus)
scavenge.text: Dense, sweet, impossibly rich. A festival food, years out of season. Eat it anyway.

scavenge.name: Tea brick
scavenge.text: Compressed tea, hard as a roof tile. Not food — morale in solid form.

scavenge.name: Cold medicine (kakkonto)
scavenge.text: Foil packets of kakkonto — the kudzu-root cold formula. For fever and stiffness, not for infections.

scavenge.name: Bandages (roll)
scavenge.text: A clean roll, still sealed. For wounds that need covering.
